Honestly I'm not even sure where to start with Arma3. I've got just over 150 hours logged at the time of writing this and I feel like I'm still scratching the surface of what this game offers. OK, so pros and cons then, let's KISS (Keep it simple,  stupid) 

Pros
- Amazing open world highly detailed military sandbox simulator 
- Tremendous modding support offering everything you could ever want from vehicles, weapons, items and equipment to game enhancements and terrains. 
- Excellent gameplay mechanics even if the controls take a little getting used to, it's pretty detailed.
- Driving/flying/boating physics are very good considering the scope of this game. 
- Land/sea/air based combat mechanics very good in base game and even better with the addition of game enhancement mods like ACE3.  
- Base maps offer good variety of terrain to get to grips with, numerous airstrips, towns, villages and other points of interest for highly involved combined arms combat scenarios. Apex DLC very reasonably priced for what it offers and makes a great addition to the base game. 
- Eden scenario editor offers full 3D drag and drop map editing with a literal fook ton of other powerful features; from dynamic  weather to complex AI scripting for creating offline and online scenarios and maps, or just to mess around in. 
- Fanbase is generally very good and supportive of new players with lots of milsim and more casual squads recruiting all the time. 
- Mods are handled via the stock game launcher so no 3rd party software is needed and is easy as he'll to do. 

Con
- Heavy on system resources. If you want consistently high fps with consistently high settings you're gonna need a decent amount of horsepower as this game demands alot from both CPU and GPU. 
- Weird/bad scripting in online servers can cause some MAD lagging
- Online can be buggy sometimes as can offline play, though I've only had it happen a couple of time where it's been bad enough for me to have to quit out and rejoin
- Occasionally the game will force close due to random errors, usually if you're running a LOT of mods. But typically it is very stable, I have about 25 mods installed and typically it runs very well (i56600k/GTX1070).
- Some of the official DLC is not great for what it costs and offers and is easily outdone by free mods. But it's a really minor point but worth mentioning nonetheless. Pick it up in a sale or as part of a bundle, then it's actually fairly good value for money

~ UPDATED: SERVER HOSTING HEADACHE
Think you gonna make a cool map and just host that so your mates can play? Nope. 

Hosting servers so you can play with your freinds and not other randoms is a NIGHTMARE to set up. It requires you to either use UPnP protocols which can put your computer at high risk (no thanks). Or you must create a static IP and manually forward ports for Aram and Steam to your router, which is a real headache. 

Think you can just do this from Control Panel? Nope again. You need to use cmd to find out all the relevent information, IPv4 and DNS Severs etc, then isolate the correct DNS primary and secondary if yours defaults to your Default Gateway, Etc etc... 

Honesly, if you're not familiar with this stuff expect to spend about 2 hours just researching and finding the info you need to do it. There is just no way to easily host a game for you and your friends right now. 
~

For the full asking price Arma3 and the Apex DLC offer potentially thousands of hours of highly enjoyable gameplay both offline and offline and many more hours of learning the powerful features of the Eden editor if that appeals to you. Right now Server Hosting is just ridiculously convenluted and honeslty I wouldn't be surprised if most people just gave up and played in public servers but the issue needs to be addressed by Bohemia as it interferes with the Apex Protocol co-op hosting as well. 

That being said, if you can pick it up in a Steam sale it is the definition of a flat out steal for the value for money it offers and the quality of the game overall. If highly detailed, super involving, super fun military land, air and sea combat simulation is your jam, so long as you don't want to host games, then Arma3 is your spoon.
